::: {.why}
Your list from last night is the start of the taxonomy this week completes, and the value of a taxonomy is that it turns a vague worry into a checklist you can test against.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name at least eight distinct look-ahead mechanisms and, for each, the test that would catch it.
- Say which two of them your existing pairs backtest is guilty of.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the taxonomy properly, expanding your list into categories: signal timing, universe construction, data revision, corporate action timing, index membership, delisting returns, parameter selection, benchmark selection, currency conversion timing, and the two that come from your own code rather than the data. Write each with a one-line detection test.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Audit your own pairs backtest against all of them. Be specific about where in the code the violation happens rather than noting the category. At least two will apply and one of them will be the formation window boundary.
:::
:::
